Description: Identified a Private Key, which may compromise cryptographic security and sensitive data encryption.
Author: Tiberiu Toca
Message:
fix(exchange): WS retry storm (1008) + Coinbase CDP credential decode

WS (the Binance 1008 'Invalid request' disconnect): subscribeTicker/
subscribeOrderBook retried every 1s forever on ANY error. A permanently
invalid symbol (e.g. a stale/junk position symbol → CCXT BadSymbol) spun
the loop, hammering the shared connection until Binance closed it with
1008, taking the valid streams down too. Now: isPermanentSubscribeError
classifies the error — permanent (BadSymbol/auth/bad-request/no-market)
logs once and STOPS that subscription; transient (network/timeout) backs
off with capped exponential delay (1s→30s) instead of fixed 1s.

Coinbase CDP / Advanced Trade keys: secret is a PEM EC private key stored
with literal \n escapes (no real newlines) → CCXT failed with 'Illegal
character at offset 30'; config also required a passphrase CDP keys don't
have. normalizePemSecret() restores real newlines for PEM secrets (no-op
for HMAC), and the passphrase is now optional (empty → omitted, required
for CDP auth; legacy Pro/OKX passphrases preserved). Verified read-only:
PEM parses, fetchTime succeeds, signed requests reach Coinbase.

Verified: tsc clean; bun test ./src/infra/exchange 107/107 (9 WS-classifier
+ 11 credential tests). Phantom GORDONTESTUSDT positions (the WS trigger)
purged from the operator DB separately.

Description: Identified a Private Key, which may compromise cryptographic security and sensitive data encryption.
Author: Tiberiu Toca
Message:
feat(audit/security): port quote-verification + value-level secret redaction (reverse-quant MIT)

Two standalone utilities from the reverse-research-funds repo (MIT) that
fit Gordon's architecture cleanly. Pure-TS ports — no Python coupling,
no MCP integration, no dependency on the rest of that repo.

1. Quote verification (src/infra/platform/audit/quoteVerification.ts)
- Anti-hallucination evidence gate. NFKD normalize → strip combining
  marks via \p{M} → collapse whitespace → casefold → substring match.
  Handles PDF reflow / accent loss / case variation that defeat strict
  equality.
- API: verifyQuote(quote, source, { method }) → boolean.
  Methods: "string_match" (default), "regex", "manual".
- Batch helper verifyQuotes() + summarizeQuoteVerifications().
- Surfaced as the verify_quote_in_text Mastra tool, wired into Gordon
  (orchestrator) + Researcher (read-only research agent that extracts
  quoted content). Agent calls it before persisting "the article says X"
  claims.

2. Value-level secret redaction (src/infra/platform/observability/valueRedaction.ts)
- Complements Gordon's existing key-name redaction in
  observability/structured.ts (SECRET_KEY_PATTERN) by covering raw
  strings where credential-shaped values can appear regardless of
  field name: alert payloads, tool error messages, news scrape,
  audit metadata blobs.
- Conservative value-format patterns: Anthropic sk-ant-api*,
  OpenAI sk-/sk-proj-, GitHub gh[pousr]_*, AWS AKIA/ASIA + prefixed
  aws_secret_access_key, Slack xox*, JWT three-segment base64url,
  Authorization Bearer headers (preserves prefix), PEM PRIVATE KEY
  blocks (RSA/EC/DSA/OPENSSH).
- API: redactValues(text) → { text, matched[], redactionCount }.
  Convenience redactString(). Deep recursive redactDeep() for
  structured values with cycle-safety + depth bound (8).
- Wired into sanitizeToolContent() in withResultSanitizer.ts so every
  tool result string passes through secret redaction in addition to
  the existing injection-pattern detection. Idempotent.

55 new tests (29 redaction + 26 quote verification), 944 framework
tests pass overall, typecheck clean.

Source: github.com/zostaff/reverse-research-funds (MIT). Provenance
clean — only the two narrow utilities were extracted; reverse-quant's
Anthropic-specific corpus / Pydantic-evidence / regulator-monitoring
infrastructure is NOT included (domain-mismatched for a trading agent).

Description: Identified a GitLab Personal Access Token, risking unauthorized access to GitLab repositories and codebase exposure.
Author: Tiberiu Toca
Message:
chore(security): pre-publish credential-pattern scanner for npm wrapper

Closes the last shippable gap from the deep npm-docs crawl. npm's
publishing guides explicitly warn:

  "Publishing sensitive information to the registry can harm your
   users, compromise your development infrastructure, be expensive
   to fix, and put you at risk of legal action."

`audit-npm-pack.cjs` audits the file LIST (whitelist of bin/, lib/,
scripts/, README.md, LICENSE). The new `audit-npm-pack-content.cjs`
audits the CONTENT of those files. A credential accidentally inlined
into bin/gordon.cjs or a JS bundle in lib/ would pass the file-list
audit but fail the content scan.

Patterns covered (15 self-test cases pass):
- npm tokens (npm_...)
- GitHub PATs (ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_)
- AWS access keys (AKIA/ASIA)
- HashiCorp Vault tokens (hvs.*)
- Stripe live + restricted-live secrets (sk_live_/rk_live_)
- OpenSSH + PEM private keys (-----BEGIN OPENSSH/* PRIVATE KEY-----)
- Slack tokens (xox*)
- GitLab PATs (glpat-*)
- Google API keys (AIza*)
- Anthropic API keys (sk-ant-api*/sk-ant-admin*)
- OpenAI API keys (sk-/sk-proj-)

Order matters in the regex list: more-specific patterns (OpenSSH
private key) come before more-general ones (generic PEM) so labels
are accurate.

Wiring:
- `npm run audit:npm-pack-content` for local invocation
- `node scripts/npm/audit-npm-pack-content.cjs --self-test` validates
  patterns without scanning real files
- release.yml `verify-npm-wrapper` job runs the scan on Linux after
  the file-list audit, gating the publish on a clean content scan
- scripts/README.md documents both the scanner and the npm publishing
  rationale for the check

Validated against the current wrapper: 7 text files scanned, 0
credential patterns detected. Run takes ~150ms.

This is the final shippable item from the npm-docs crawl (~75 pages
across cli/v11/* + configuring-npm + most of using-npm + security +
integrations + packages-and-modules). No further shippable items
remain — outstanding pages are tutorials and beginner-onboarding
content with zero security relevance for Gordon.
